## Summary

**Root cause** — `DocumentIO.saveDocument()` decided whether to write the file by comparing the editor text against the *in-memory history's initial version*:

```java
Document documentInitial = document.getInitialVersion();
if (!currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())) { ...write... } else { ret = true; }  // silently no-op
```

`Document.getInitialVersion()` returns `_history.get(0)`, but **the editor history is disabled by default** (`AppSettings.isEditorHistoryEnabled()` → `false`), so `_history` stays empty and the "initial version" is only snapshotted lazily *inside* `saveDocument` — from the **already-modified** document. The snapshot therefore contains the current text, `currentText.equals(initial.getContent())` is `true`, and **nothing is ever written** while `saveDocument` reports success.

This matches the report exactly:
- `DocumentEditFragment.onContentEditValueChanged()` copies the editor text into the `Document` only after a 5 s delay (`HISTORY_DELTA`) — the same moment the save icon becomes enabled.
- Waiting for the icon ⇒ content already in the `Document` ⇒ the bogus snapshot ⇒ save skipped, and every later save (back press/`onPause`) skips too ⇒ **note never created**.
- Pressing back immediately (steps 3–4 skipped) ⇒ content not yet in the `Document` ⇒ snapshot is empty ⇒ file written ⇒ works.

**Fix** (`DocumentIO.saveDocument`): decide by comparing with what is *actually on disk*, and track the rename source via the document's previous file instead of the unreliable history entry. An untouched, never-stored document still creates no file, and unchanged files are still not rewritten.

Also hardened `DocumentEditFragment.saveDocument()` to point its arguments at the real file once stored, so the "new note in folder" arguments can no longer make `checkReloadDisk()` replace the saved note with a fresh empty document.

**Verification** (Gradle can't run here — it fails at dependency download, identically before/after my change, since this environment has no network):
- Compiled every source file with `javac` against the Android 27 SDK: both modified files compile cleanly, and the error set is byte-identical to the unpatched baseline (56 pre-existing errors, all in unrelated files due to missing third-party jars offline).
- Ran the reported scenario end-to-end against the real compiled `DocumentIO`/`Document` classes: unpatched → note not created (4 failures incl. silent loss of edits to existing notes); patched → all pass, with both history settings.
- Added `app/src/test/java/net/gsantner/markor/util/DocumentIoTest.java` (7 tests): fails 4/7 on the old code, passes 7/7 on the fixed code; the existing `DocumentTest` suite still passes.
